a24_2_cost.allocation: shared / arm-specific preparation rows (practice.jsonl, priced as Gemma since practice is Gemma-planned, and optional prep_cost.jsonl rows, which must name cost_kind gemma / api / codex): a row with `arm` (or `arms`) goes to those arms, a row without goes to the consumer arms under allocation_rule; each arm's allocated total is spread equally over its attempted presentations. Planning seconds of a prep row = planning_s or plan_secs (never the episode wall_s). A Gemma prep row without a validated measurement makes its targets' cost UNKNOWN (energy_method.unmeasured_rule; practice-v2 has no energy measurement)

allocation_rule.meaning: split: each shared row is allocated ONCE, divided among its target arms in proportion to their registered workload (the cohort presentations; equal workloads -> equal shares; with all 8 main arms the practice consumers are G+M, O+M, X+M, G+FS, O+FS = one fifth each; Astra P-cost Q1/Q2). full (each target carries the whole row) duplicates shared expenditure and is not reported. practice_required: consumer arms without any practice / preparation row are UNKNOWN

arm_kinds.api: O* (and archived S* / H*): cost_usd of the plan journal (dated list prices; reasoning and repairs included, cache replays cost 0)
arm_kinds.codex: X*: CLI planning NOT priced (subscription: no incremental API expenditure; A24.2 prices local Gemma and API arms only); its allocated preparation USD is kept and reported, its total stays incomplete, never zero
arm_kinds.gemma: G*: energy + hardware allocation (+ any cost_usd); a Gemma row without an energy figure (energy_j_gpu) makes the arm's cost UNKNOWN unless the practice-row estimate applies

a24_2_cost.ci: 95 % percentile interval (inverted-CDF order statistics, no interpolation), task-family cluster bootstrap, B = 20000, seed = final_test_power.SEED; ONE resampling matrix over the union of families for every arm, view and ratio

claim.rule: permitted only when the lower 95 % bound of R >= 0.80 AND the upper 95 % bound of C <= 0.10, both obtainable and finite, in a complete study, with G+M and O0 covering the cohort, and (real data) with freeze.json a24_2_cost recorded including the hardware price basis; A24.2 makes this the statement available when H1 is not established; otherwise estimates and CIs only
claim.text: Gemma with the package retained at least 80% of unassisted Opus's success rate at at most 10% of its specified planning cost

a24_2_cost.codex_pareto_exception: documented exception to 'showing all arms' (Astra P-cost Q6; no subscription allocation rule is registered): X arms appear in the Pareto table and under the plot with their SR and known preparation USD, without a cost coordinate. A subscription allocation would have to be fixed prospectively (PENDING ARASH if wanted)
a24_2_cost.cohort: the registered task cohort = every (item, language) presentation scored in any arm, minus INVALID presentations (dropped from every arm). Every outcome uses the same item weights: item value = mean over its cohort presentations; an arm missing a cohort presentation is reported (missing_vs_cohort), never silently dropped, and blocks the reading rule if it is G+M or O0

energy_method.accuracy: approximate: a mean of about 10 readings per second times the time; no calibration, no coverage or gap checks; the readings are the driver's own power figure, not an external meter
energy_method.code: sim/final_test/matrix/energy.py, installed for one launch (energy.measuring) on plan.Plan._call_cell by matrix_run.py (plan phase) and planfirst.py; mandatory in test-v1 (planning is refused when nvidia-smi cannot be read). plan.py is not edited
energy_method.decision: Arash, 2026-10-14 (docs/final-test/progress.md 'ARASH DECISION: simplify the energy method (C5)'): measure the GPU's average power draw with nvidia-smi during Gemma planning, multiply by the planning time, price it at 0.20 USD/kWh; drop the coverage / gap / backwards-clock checks; disclose it plainly as a simple, approximate method
energy_method.disclosure: Planning energy is a simple, approximate figure: the GPU's average power draw reported by nvidia-smi (about 10 readings per second) during each Gemma planning call, multiplied by the planning time and priced at 0.20 USD/kWh. Only the GPU is counted (CPU and the rest of the laptop are not), so it understates total energy; idle power is included. The 10 practice rows that ran before the meter existed are estimated from the measured rate and flagged.
energy_method.join: analyze.attach_energy: a Gemma plan row takes energy_j_gpu and planning_s from the one energy row whose bound plan line sha256 equals the sha256 of its plan journal line; no such row (or several) -> no energy figure -> UNKNOWN cost
energy_method.journal: energy.jsonl (energy.<pass id>.jsonl for --pass-id runs) beside plan.jsonl: one 'open' row per run (GPU name, idle mean) and one 'cell' row per Gemma cell, bound to its plan journal line by sha256
energy_method.method: a background nvidia-smi (--query-gpu=power.draw.instant -i 0 -lms 100) prints the GPU board power about every 100 ms for the whole plan phase. Per Gemma plan cell: planning_s = the time from just before plan.Plan._call_cell starts to just after it returns (every attempt, repair and parse of that cell); gpu_w_mean = the plain mean of the readings that arrived in that time (none there: the readings within 1 s of it); energy_j_gpu = gpu_w_mean x planning_s; USD = energy_j_gpu / 3,600,000 x usd_per_kwh. A cell with no reading at all has no energy figure (its cost is UNKNOWN)
energy_method.not_measured: GPU only: the CPU, memory, display, storage, fans and power-supply losses are NOT measured (energy_j_cpu is None), so the figure is LOWER than the laptop's total planning energy. The reading is the whole GPU board (every process on it, the idle floor included, never subtracted); the idle floor measured when the meter opens is reported

unmeasured_estimate.definition: rate_w = (sum of the measured energy_j_gpu) / (sum of their planning_s) over every Gemma plan row of the analysed run with an energy figure from the join (never estimates): the average measured Gemma GPU power per planning second; an eligible practice row's estimate = rate_w x its own planning seconds (planning_s / plan_secs; none -> UNKNOWN), assuming the measured and the earlier calls draw comparable power (same laptop, same model). Only the 10 practice-v2 rows named in the terms (bound to practice.jsonl by sha) are eligible
unmeasured_estimate.disclosure: reported per arm: measured joules (primary), estimated rows / seconds / joules / USD and the rate (n cells, seconds); markdown labels the estimate
unmeasured_estimate.too_few: fewer than min_cells measured rows (or zero measured seconds) -> no rate -> the practice rows stay UNKNOWN

energy_method.unmeasured_rule: the 10 practice-v2 rows ran before the meter existed. On Arash's decision of 2026-10-14 ('energy estimate ok') each is ESTIMATED as the run's measured Gemma rate x the row's own planning seconds and flagged 'estimated'; the measured figure stays the primary one and the estimate is disclosed beside it. Every other Gemma row without an energy figure keeps an UNKNOWN cost

a24_2_cost.energy_requirement: the producer takes the mean GPU power over the SAME interval that gives the planning seconds (energy_method c5-simple-1); the energy method is recorded in freeze.json
a24_2_cost.energy_rule: GPU energy in joules (plan row energy_j_gpu = nvidia-smi mean power x planning_s) / 3,600,000 x usd_per_kwh (energy_method)
a24_2_cost.hardware_price_disclosure: A33: planning time is measured on the run laptop (RTX 4060, 8 GB). The headline hardware allocation combines those measured hours with the USD 399 reference-device price. The energy term is the laptop GPU's energy during planning (energy_method c5-simple-1: nvidia-smi average power x planning time; GPU only, approximate). A Gemma plan row without an energy figure stays UNKNOWN and blocks the A24.2 statement. Sensitivity: the hw_time_3x row (3 x planning hours, laptop energy held fixed; factor 3 = an approved sensitivity assumption, not a measured slowdown); the reading rule uses the headline view only
a24_2_cost.hardware_price_source: reference price, prereg A33 (2026-10-14, Arash decision 8; prospectively replaces A24.2's 'declared laptop purchase price'): NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit 8 GB, USD 399 (ledger 2026-10-12 'Hardware price for A24.2'); a reference device price, not the run laptop's price, and not shown to run this system; recorded in freeze.json as a24_2_cost before the first test call
a24_2_cost.hardware_price_status: recorded: prereg A33 (prospective; approved by Arash 2026-10-14, decision 8; signature pending at the freeze summary). D13 is closed. freeze.json a24_2_cost must carry this basis; the freeze builder checks that the A33 heading exists in the prereg
a24_2_cost.hardware_rule: hardware_price_usd / operating_hours x attributable planning hours
a24_2_cost.hardware_time_note: view hw_time_3x = '3x hardware-time sensitivity; measured laptop energy held fixed' (ledger 2026-10-12: a Jetson-class device plans more slowly). It is NOT an estimate of Jetson energy or of total operating cost
a24_2_cost.operating_hours_rule: three years at 2,000 operating hours / year

outcomes.a: total planning USD / successful tasks per arm = sum of item-mean cost / sum of item-mean SR (equal to presentation totals / successes under complete EN/FA coverage); the raw totals are reported too
outcomes.b: R = SR(G+M) / SR(O0) and C = mean planning USD per attempted task G+M / O0, item-weighted on the cohort
outcomes.c: Pareto data: item-weighted SR against mean planning USD per attempted task, all arms (pareto.svg beside analysis.json)
outcomes.latency: planning seconds per attempted task including repairs and failed attempts (mean, median, p90)

a24_2_cost.planning_seconds: plan row planning_s if present, else wall_s (the plan cell's wall time: every sequential attempt, repair and failed attempt, counted once; never both the cell interval and its attempts); no other fallback (a sum of request latencies would omit parsing, retrieval and package time) -> a Gemma row without either is UNKNOWN
a24_2_cost.scope: planning cost only (executor / simulator excluded); CIs describe task-sampling uncertainty conditional on these prices and assumptions
a24_2_cost.undefined_rule: a ratio with denominator 0 is +infinity when the numerator is > 0 and UNDEFINED when it is 0 (point estimate and every bootstrap replicate). Infinite replicates stay in the ordering; if ANY replicate is undefined, or a needed cost is unknown, the CI bounds are 'not obtainable' (reported with the counts, never dropped) and the reading rule cannot be satisfied

views.hardware_only: the hardware allocation alone (per arm only; no C is formed for it)
views.headline: API USD + energy + hardware + allocated
views.hw_time_3x: 3x hardware-time sensitivity; measured laptop energy held fixed

a24_2_cost.workload: scored cells only: every plan row of (arm, canon presentation, r = 0, block main or unset) is summed (all incurred attempts); plan rows of other blocks (REPEAT r > 0, curve, relocation) are totalled separately and are not in the per-task outcomes

a36.eligibility: excluded_reset (a36.excluded_reset, computed in score.py): a core cell (block main, canon, r0, run0) whose final class is infra_exec and whose 3 attempts (0, 1, 2) of the CURRENT epoch (latest of the executor's epoch state, rows and starts) each started once (exec_attempt_start) and stopped at the pre-execution reset gate (status blocked_state, registered comparison failed, not overridden, prims == sweep prims, 0 action-resolve, no error, no outcome); anything mixed, malformed or missing -> not flagged
a36.h1: h1_rule_c7 unchanged (K >= 20 guard; K < 20 -> inconclusive); its validation did not cover this selection step
a36.per_arm_sr: item-weighted (analyze.arm_rates) over non-flagged cells; item and presentation denominators printed
a36.registered_alongside: A21: infra_exec = SR 0 in every denominator; differences between the two analyses are named
a36.reset_limited: an arm with MORE than 5% of its core cells flagged labels every contrast involving it
a36.retention: paired common subset per contrast: a presentation flagged in EITHER arm leaves both; then the registered aggregation (per item the mean of retained EN/FA differences, equal item weights, empty items / families dropped, K and N recomputed); every contrast (H1, Holm m = 3, exploratory H4a-b / H5a-c, equivalence E1); exploratory stays exploratory
a36.status: SIGNED (Arash, 2026-10-15; signatures.json key A36; A36-DRAFT.md r2); binds the locked test once the freeze records it
a36.unavailable: fewer than 2 retained families -> the contrast is unavailable: H1 / E1 inconclusive (no claim), a Holm member enters with p = 1 and m stays 3; counts are explicit zeros

dependence.cluster: the 42 test families (paired: every arm of a family moves together)
dependence.shared_executions: plan cells with equal execution-unit keys share one simulator run; their outcome is ONE realisation. The family cluster contains every unit, so the intervals and tests already treat copies as dependent; the report adds the number of independent executions and a sensitivity that drops presentations where the two arms of a contrast share a unit (that estimate is performance CONDITIONAL on non-shared executions: it changes the population and cannot validate or replace the full-sample result)
dependence.unit_of_analysis: item (mean of its EN and FA presentations)

h1.decision: A24.1: h1-rule-1 = C7 (final_test_h1_stats.h1_rule_c7): CR2 + Satterthwaite, guard K >= 20 discordant families, one-sided computational level .0175 per tail (nominal 96.5 % interval); NI iff L > -.05; superior iff NI and L > 0 (fixed sequence); materially inferior iff U < -.05; 'statistically lower' iff NI and U < 0; se = 0 / undefined df / guard failure -> inconclusive. The registered wild+percentile rule (final_test_power.h1_decision) failed its validation and is never used for a claim
h1.estimation_only_if: H1_PROCEDURE['validated'] is False (then estimate + interval only, no NI / superior / inferior wording)
h1.exploratory_equivalence: E1 (G+M vs O+M): CR2 + Satterthwaite 90 % interval + guard K >= 20, inside +/-5 pp; exploratory only
h1.family: none -- H1 stands alone; it is NOT a member of the Holm family
h1.validation: docs/final-test/h1_validation/v100_summary.C7.json (226 configurations x 100,000 datasets, 0/628 null cells above the frozen gate)
h1.views: primary = item-weighted (validated); family-weighted and infra-paired = sensitivities (same rule, not separately validated)

holm.note: m = 3 since A24.5 (H2a, H2c, H3a; all superiority or two-sided, no non-inferiority member); H4a-b and H5a-c are EXPLORATORY (raw p, listed in `exploratory`); H2b, H3b and H3c are WITHDRAWN (Sonnet is archived, A23), their IDs are kept in `withdrawn`; the smaller m relaxes the Holm thresholds, which is disclosed (the report prints the m = 8 adjustment of the A23 family next to the m = 3 verdict)

H3c.meaning: Gemma+memory non-inferior to Sonnet without memory

ni_guard.effect: applied to NO m = 3 Holm member (none is a non-inferiority test); retained for the m = 8 transparency comparison, where H5c's p is set to 1 (not rejected)
ni_guard.residual: no inflation above nominal was seen in the grid once the guard applies (largest rates are at or below nominal within Monte Carlo error); NI claims from H5c are still labelled approximate
ni_guard.scope: H5c only, and only inside the m = 8 transparency comparison (A24.5 made H5c exploratory); NOT H1, whose registered calibration table (section 9.6) is unchanged
ni_guard.why: docs/final-test/matrix/ni_calibration.json: type-I error of the complete non-inferiority procedure at the null boundary D = -5 pp, 4,000 simulations per cell (Monte Carlo SE about .001), discordance .05-.30, family ICC 0 / .3 / .6; without the guard the first-Holm-step rate (nominal p1 < .00227) is up to .14 at discordance .05, .054 at .10, .027 at .15, .009 at .20 and .0075 at .25; with the guard at .25 the largest first-step rate in the grid is .0022 and the largest rate at the most lenient step (nominal .025) is .0213; guards at .20 and .15 left .0037 and .0047

p_values.greater: one-sided wild cluster bootstrap, null imposed at delta0 (0 for superiority)
p_values.ni_x2: H5c (EXPLORATORY since A24.5): p1 = one-sided wild test of H0: D <= -5 pp (the null BOUNDARY is imposed, not 0), reported raw; min(1, 2 p1) with the guard only in the m = 8 transparency comparison; never from a test of D = 0

sensitivities: infra_paired (planner transport failure OR execution infrastructure failure of either arm)

plan.cluster: the 42 test families (paired: every arm of a family moves together)
plan.shared_executions: plan cells with equal execution-unit keys share one simulator run; their outcome is ONE realisation. The family cluster contains every unit, so the intervals and tests already treat copies as dependent; the report adds the number of independent executions and a sensitivity that drops presentations where the two arms of a contrast share a unit (that estimate is performance CONDITIONAL on non-shared executions: it changes the population and cannot validate or replace the full-sample result)
